mac_bookseller.text: Scotland's National Book Town, and I run the smallest shop in it. A customer buys a book here and I know the title and their dog's name.
Fàilte, and mind the step. The step is the best-read in the building.

mac_prior.text: St Ninian came to Whithorn about 397, they say, and built a white stone church. Pilgrims have been walking here ever since. I took the bus for the last bit, to be honest.
Beannachd leibh, that is 'blessings with you', which is what the monks would say as you left. They did not say it if you left with the silverware.

mac_kite.text: A red kite has a forked tail and a very elegant way of showing off. Back in the nineteenth century they were all but gone. Now you can count them on a good day.
I have watched them since they were let go. I like to think they remember me. They do not.

mac_farmer.text: The Machars is a place where nothing happens, slowly, in a very green way. I would not live anywhere else, because nowhere else would put up with me.
If a bookshop and a priory and a kite all turn up in one afternoon, that is a good day on the Machars.

mac_kite_c.text: A hootlet, sleepy and wide-eyed, sits on a book shelf in a window and looks very much like it is reading.
